name: Dysostosis with Brachydactyly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Dysostosis with Brachydactyly

criteria.description: Presence of brachydactyly characterized by shortened phalanges and metacarpals
Radiological evidence of dysostosis including abnormal bone formation and segmentation defects
Onset of skeletal abnormalities present at birth or early infancy
Lack of significant involvement of other organ systems such as cardiovascular or neurological

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of brachydactyly with radiological confirmation of dysostosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital brachydactyly with shortened metacarpals and phalanges
searchTerms: born with short fingers and hand bones

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radiographic evidence of dysostosis with abnormal bone segmentation

common.symptomName: Short stature due to skeletal dysplasia
searchTerms: short height caused by bone growth disorders
below average stature due to skeletal issues

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in affected digits
Mild facial dysmorphism including midface hypoplasia
Delayed bone age on radiological assessment

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness in peripheral joints
searchTerms: mild stiffness in joints of hands or feet
holes or defects in heart walls

rare.symptomName: Respiratory complications due to thoracic cage abnormalities
searchTerms: lung issues due to rib cage

imaging: X-ray showing brachydactyly with shortened metacarpals and phalanges
Radiographs demonstrating dysostosis with abnormal bone segmentation and delayed bone age
genetic: Possible mutations in genes involved in skeletal development (specific gene not well defined)
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic hand abnormalities and short stature

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of osteolysis rather than congenital shortening

redFlags: Progressive worsening of skeletal deformities beyond infancy
Presence of neurological deficits or developmental delay
Cardiopulmonary compromise due to thoracic cage abnormalities
references: Pagon RA et al. GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2023.
